text: When this janitor died, his town found out he was worth eight million dollars.
Ronald Read pumped gas for twenty-five years, then cleaned a department store for seventeen more.
He drove a used car and held his coat together with a safety pin.
Once, a stranger at a diner paid for his breakfast, thinking he couldn't afford it.
His secret? He kept buying shares of boring companies. Soap. Medicine. Electricity.
He reinvested every dividend and held on for decades.
When he died, he left one point two million dollars to the town library, and four point eight million to the hospital.
No lottery. No crypto. Just spend less than you earn, buy what lasts, and wait.
